result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say the designer is partly right, recommend a simplified mark with no tagline, and keep the work small with three logo versions. B names more concrete causes, including minimum gap spacing, stretch in polo knit and auto-digitizing from a JPG or PNG, and adds practical details such as chest size, sample cost and questions to ask the designer. A covers the same ground with slightly less detail on why things fail. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give nearly the same core advice: the designer is partly right, make a simplified mark without the tagline, use a monogram for the favicon, get the logo re-digitized with a sample stitch-out, and keep a one-page usage sheet. A covers causes slightly better because it mentions small gaps and stretchy knit. B wins narrowly: it scopes the job more clearly to a small firm, adds a light and dark browser-theme check, and says plainly that it hasn't seen the logo.
